body:
Introduction to the National Quantum Mission

The National Quantum Mission (NQM) is an initiative of the Government of India to develop scientific research, technological capabilities and an innovation ecosystem in quantum technologies.

The Union Cabinet approved the mission on 19 April 2023. It is implemented by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) under the Government of India.

The mission supports research and development in quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing and metrology, and quantum materials and devices.

National Quantum Mission: Core facts

  • Approval: 19 April 2023.
  • Approved total outlay: Rs. 6,003.65 crore.
  • Mission period: Financial years 2023–24 to 2030–31.
  • Duration: 8 years.
  • Implementing department: Department of Science and Technology, Government of India.
  • Major research areas: 4 quantum-technology domains.

The mission seeks to encourage indigenous technological development, strengthen research institutions, support startups, build a skilled workforce and promote cooperation between academic institutions and industry.

Major objectives of the mission

1. Quantum computing

One of the mission's important targets is the development of intermediate-scale quantum computers containing 50–1,000 physical qubits over the 8-year mission period.

The mission supports research on different physical platforms, including superconducting and photonic technologies.

The expression physical qubit refers to a physical quantum-information unit used in a quantum processor. It should not be confused with a fully protected logical qubit built using error-correction methods. A target expressed in physical qubits is therefore not a guarantee of error-free computation.

The figure of 50–1,000 physical qubits is a development target, not a statement that India had already achieved every level of this capability when the mission was approved.

2. Quantum communication

Quantum communication uses quantum-mechanical properties to support information-transfer and security applications.

The mission includes the development of:

  • Satellite-based secure quantum communication between ground stations separated by distances of about 2,000 km within India.
  • Long-distance secure quantum communication with other countries.
  • Inter-city quantum key distribution over distances of about 2,000 km.
  • Multi-node quantum networks using quantum memories.

Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a technique for establishing shared secret cryptographic keys using quantum states. Interception or disturbance of the transmitted quantum information can, under suitable protocol conditions, produce detectable changes.

QKD helps with the distribution of encryption keys. It does not itself mean that the data are being processed by a quantum computer.

3. Quantum sensing and metrology

Quantum sensing uses quantum properties to make measurements of physical quantities with high sensitivity or precision.

Metrology is the science of measurement. It includes developing and maintaining accurate measurement standards.

Mission objectives in this field include high-sensitivity magnetometers and atomic clocks.

  • Magnetometers: Instruments that measure magnetic fields.
  • Atomic clocks: Highly precise clocks that use characteristic atomic transitions as frequency references.

Such technologies can support accurate timing, navigation and scientific measurement.

4. Quantum materials and devices

This area concerns materials and physical devices used to develop quantum technologies.

It includes research on superconducting materials, novel semiconductor structures, single-photon sources, photon detectors and other components relevant to quantum systems.

Quantum materials and devices support the development of quantum computers, communication systems and sensors. They are therefore related to, but distinct from, the other mission areas.

The 4 Thematic Hubs

The National Quantum Mission established 4 Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs) during financial year 2024–25. Each hub focuses on a major quantum-technology area.

Thematic HubHost institutionLocation
Quantum ComputingIndian Institute of Science (IISc)Bengaluru, Karnataka
Quantum CommunicationIIT Madras, in association with C-DOTChennai, Tamil Nadu
Quantum Sensing and MetrologyIIT BombayMumbai, Maharashtra
Quantum Materials and DevicesIIT DelhiNew Delhi, Delhi

The hubs bring together universities, research institutions, scientists, industry participants and startups. Their role includes technology development, building research infrastructure, supporting entrepreneurship and developing human resources.

The 4 hub locations should not be confused with the locations of every institution participating in the mission. NQM is a national initiative involving institutions across different states.

Mission timeline and implementation status

The approved mission period runs from 2023–24 to 2030–31. Individual research targets and institutional activities are implemented over this period.

A government parliamentary reply dated 12 August 2026, describing developments during 2025–26, reported that the 4 Thematic Hubs had been operationalized. It also reported the following implementation activities:

  • 14 Technical Groups and 17 Project Teams associated with the Thematic Hubs.
  • Research infrastructure facilities being established at IISc Bengaluru, IIT Bombay, IIT Kanpur and IIT Delhi.
  • 23 Quantum Teaching Laboratories being established across the country.
  • Support extended to 17 quantum-technology startups.

These are government-reported implementation figures for the stated reporting period. They are not the same as the long-term scientific targets of the mission.

At the 5 November 2026 content cutoff, the mission remained within its approved implementation period. Its 2030–31 completion horizon had not yet been reached. Consequently, the complete 8-year research targets should not be described as already achieved.

Gujarat's connection with quantum technologies

Gujarat has relevant quantum-technology research, education and communication initiatives. These developments illustrate how quantum science can connect with institutions and applications beyond the 4 national Thematic Hub locations.

Quantum communication demonstration in Gandhinagar

On the night of 27–28 September 2026, QNu Labs, the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N) and IIT Gandhinagar conducted a free-space quantum key distribution demonstration.

The demonstration established a 5.56 km free-space QKD link between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology announced the result through the Press Information Bureau on 3 October 2026.

Free-space means that the optical quantum communication link operates through open space rather than requiring an optical fibre along the communication path.

The demonstration was concerned with quantum communication and secure key distribution, not with building a general-purpose quantum computer or proving computational quantum advantage.

The reported field trial is a completed demonstration. It should not be confused with the National Quantum Mission's longer-distance communication targets, which have different technical and geographic requirements.

Gujarat Quantum Transformation Programme

Gujarat Informatics Limited issued a request for proposal dated 14 September 2026 under the Gujarat Quantum Transformation Programme.

The request concerned establishing, implementing, operating and maintaining a Quantum Communication Lab, together with designing and conducting a faculty development programme.

The published procurement notice establishes that such an initiative was being pursued. However, a tender notice alone does not establish that the proposed laboratory had already become operational.

This initiative is distinct from the Union Government's National Quantum Mission, although both concern the development of quantum-technology capabilities.

Quantum-technology education in Gujarat

The Institute of Infrastructure, Technology, Research and Management (IITRAM) in Ahmedabad describes a Minor Programme in Quantum Technologies aligned with the National Quantum Mission and AICTE guidelines.

Its stated curriculum comprises 18 credits and introduces quantum computing, communication, sensing and materials. This illustrates the educational and workforce-development dimension of the quantum-technology ecosystem.

Connecting the concepts with the mission

The National Quantum Mission is easier to understand when its different activities are connected with the basic principles of quantum information:

  • Qubit: The basic quantum-information unit used in quantum computing.
  • Superposition: Allows a quantum state to contain coherent combinations of basis states.
  • Entanglement: Allows quantum subsystems to share nonseparable joint states.
  • Quantum interference: Allows operations to reinforce or suppress possible measurement outcomes.
  • Quantum advantage: Describes superior quantum-computing performance on a specified task under an appropriate comparison.
  • National Quantum Mission: Supports the development of quantum technologies, research infrastructure, institutions and skilled human resources in India.

The 4 mission areas have different purposes. Quantum computing processes information; quantum communication focuses on transferring quantum information and supporting communication security; quantum sensing improves measurements; and quantum materials and devices provide important physical foundations.

All 4 draw on quantum mechanics, but progress in 1 area does not automatically establish success in the others.

Prelims focus

  • National Quantum Mission: approved on 19 April 2023 and implemented by DST.
  • Approved outlay: Rs. 6,003.65 crore for 2023–24 to 2030–31.
  • Quantum-computing target: development of systems with 50–1,000 physical qubits over 8 years.
  • 4 T-Hubs: IISc Bengaluru, IIT Madras with C-DOT, IIT Bombay and IIT Delhi.
  • Gujarat: BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar participated in a 5.56 km free-space QKD demonstration on 27–28 September 2026 with QNu Labs.
  • Trap: NQM targets, completed demonstrations and proposals for new facilities are 3 different implementation statuses.

[Sources: Press Information Bureau, Cabinet release 'Cabinet Approves National Quantum Mission to Scale-up Scientific and Industrial Research and Development for Quantum Technologies', 19 April 2023; Department of Science and Technology, 'National Quantum Mission (NQM)', mission objectives and thematic areas, consulted 5 November 2026; Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Science and Technology, 'Parliament Question: National Quantum Mission', 12 August 2026, progress during 2025–26; Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, 'India's First 5.56 km Free-Space Quantum Key Distribution Link Demonstrated', 3 October 2026; Gujarat Informatics Limited, Tender GEM/2026/B/8018319, dated 14 September 2026, Gujarat Quantum Transformation Programme; IITRAM, 'Quantum Technologies', Minor Programme description, consulted 5 November 2026.]
